title.en: Distinguish international business from domestic business

say.en: Coffee grown in Chikkamagaluru is drunk in Italy, while the phone in your pocket may have parts from five countries. Why do nations trade with each other? In this lesson: Define international business.
Explain why nations trade.
Distinguish international business from domestic business.

body.en: *International business* refers to manufacturing and trade activities that cross national frontiers. It is wider than international trade: besides exports and imports of goods and services, it includes licensing and franchising, contract manufacturing and foreign investment. Nations trade because natural resources are unequally distributed, labour productivity and production costs differ due to differences in factors such as skills, technology and climate, and so each nation gains by specialising in what it can produce at a comparatively lower cost and trading for the rest.
body.kn: ಅಂತರರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ಗಡಿಗಳನ್ನು ದಾಟುತ್ತದೆ. ಸಂಪನ್ಮೂಲ ಮತ್ತು ಉತ್ಪಾದನಾ ವೆಚ್ಚ ದೇಶದಿಂದ ದೇಶಕ್ಕೆ ಭಿನ್ನವಾದ್ದರಿಂದ ದೇಶಗಳು ವ್ಯಾಪಾರ ಮಾಡುತ್ತವೆ.

Why trade? Resources and costs differ. If India makes textiles cheaper and Japan makes electronics cheaper, both gain by specialising and trading.
How does it differ from domestic business?
Customers vary across markets, each country has its own rules and tariffs, and more than one currency is used, so risk is higher.

explanation.en: International business deals with different nationalities, currencies, laws, political systems and customer tastes, so it is more complex and riskier.

say.en: Sort each feature: domestic business or international business.
say.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಲಕ್ಷಣವನ್ನು ದೇಶೀಯ ಅಥವಾ ಅಂತರರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ವ್ಯವಹಾರ ಎಂದು ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

body.en: International business differs from *domestic business* in: nationality of buyers and sellers (different countries), nationality of other stakeholders such as employees and investors, mobility of factors of production (much less mobile between countries), customer heterogeneity across markets, differences in business systems and practices, political systems and risks, business regulations and policies such as tariffs and quotas, and the currency used (more than one currency, with exchange rate risk). As a result, international business is more complex and riskier.
body.kn: ದೇಶೀಯ ವ್ಯವಹಾರಕ್ಕೆ ಹೋಲಿಸಿದರೆ ಅಂತರರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯ ವ್ಯವಹಾರವು ಬೇರೆ ಬೇರೆ ರಾಷ್ಟ್ರೀಯತೆ, ಕರೆನ್ಸಿ, ಕಾನೂನು ಮತ್ತು ಸಂಪ್ರದಾಯಗಳನ್ನು ಎದುರಿಸುವುದರಿಂದ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಸಂಕೀರ್ಣ ಮತ್ತು ಅಪಾಯಕರ.

answer.en: The exporter receives ₹1,00,000 less because of the change in exchange rate.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. A Mangaluru cashew exporter signs a contract to sell to a US buyer for $50,000 when the exchange rate is ₹83 per dollar. When payment arrives, the rate is ₹81 per dollar. Find the rupee amount at both rates and the effect on the exporter.

say.en: Let us work through this together. A Mangaluru cashew exporter signs a contract to sell to a US buyer for $50,000 when the exchange rate is 83 rupees per dollar. When payment arrives, the rate is 81 rupees per dollar. Find the rupee amount at both rates and the effect on the exporter.
At contract: 50,000 times 83 rupees equals 41,50,000 rupees.
At payment: 50,000 times 81 rupees equals 40,50,000 rupees.
Difference equals 41,50,000 rupees minus 40,50,000 rupees equals 1,00,000 rupees less received.
Domestic sales carry no such currency risk: this shows why international business is riskier.
So the answer is The exporter receives 1,00,000 rupees less because of the change in exchange rate.

say.en: Now try questions in the pattern of the CUET entrance test. An Indian exporter invoices goods for $5,000 when $1 equals 82 rupees. When payment arrives, $1 equals 80 rupees. Compared with what was expected at the time of the deal, the exporter receives.
Expected 82 rupees times 5,000 equals 4,10,000 rupees; received 80 rupees times 5,000 equals 4,00,000 rupees; so 10,000 rupees less.
This is exchange-rate risk.
